issues.legal_issue: Affixation of a recovery notice after personal tender is refused can constitute sufficient service when the affected party was aware of the recovery and proposed sale.
material_facts: A recovery officer attached and auctioned the firm's property to recover unpaid sales tax.
The process-server reported that a partner of the firm had refused to accept the notice before it was affixed.
Other reports showed that the partners had refused notices sent in connection with the recovery proceedings.
The partners knew of the attachment and proposed auction, and a partner admitted in a letter that he had received notice of the auction.
The firm's counsel had sought time to pay the tax due, but the amount remained unpaid after time was granted.
issues.conclusion: The objection that service by affixation failed to comply with the prescribed procedure was not well-founded, and there was no valid ground to interfere with the dismissal of the writ petition. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Rules 11–14 governing service by revenue officers and revenue courts, notice is ordinarily served personally or on a recognised agent; other prescribed modes apply when the person cannot be found, and affixation is permitted when service cannot be effected by the preceding methods. In this case, the refusal to accept tender, together with evidence of actual awareness and admitted receipt of the auction notice, supported the conclusion that service by affixation did not invalidate the recovery proceedings. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: recovery_sale_writ_appeal and notice_tender_refused and notice_affixed_after_refusal and affected_party_aware_of_sale

predicates.recovery_sale_writ_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from dismissal of a writ petition challenging attachment and sale in a tax-recovery process.
predicates.notice_tender_refused: A person connected with the affected party refused to accept a notice when it was tendered.
predicates.notice_affixed_after_refusal: The serving officer affixed the notice after the tender was refused.
predicates.affected_party_aware_of_sale: The affected party knew of the attachment and proposed sale, including through an admission that auction notice had been received.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a writ challenge to a recovery sale, the notice was refused and then affixed, and the affected party knew of the sale, the service objection is rejected.
